content:
We have the RSS channel listing all commits, but I thought it would be nice to have a thread highlighting bigger results that have landed in CSLib after a series of PRs. Here are a few I'm aware of from the past couple of weeks:

  • cslib#329: ω-regular languages are closed under complementation by @Ching-Tsun Chou
  • cslib#411: strong normalization for the simply typed lambda calculus by @David Wegmann
  • cslib#456: confluence for βη-reduction of untyped lambda calculus by @Maximiliano Onofre Martínez

Thank you all for your contributions!

The result about the closure of ω-regular languages under complementation is a reincarnation of a major part of my earlier automata theory project:
https://github.com/ctchou/AutomataTheory
Compared with that earlier project, I think the CSLib version has a much better treatment of ωSequence, which now has a pretty decent API. Also, CSLib's automata theory is built on top of LTS and hence shares the same infrastructure with other state-transition-based models of computation such as process algebras and temporal logics.
